title: Recast of the Installment on Home Mortgage Loans After a Large Principal Curtailment
content:
A recast on a Home Mortgage Loans note re-amortizes the remaining principal over the remaining term at the note rate. It lowers the principal and interest payment and changes neither the note rate nor the maturity date.

## What a recast calls for

1. The program must be one on which a recast is offered.
2. The extra principal payments made since the last recast must total at least the program's stated curtailment total. Where the loan has never been recast, the total is taken from the funding date; where it has, from the date of the last recast. It is the sum of the principal part of those extra principal payments, taken from the loan's own payment records through the measurement date.
3. The loan must be active and current.

The program's recast fee is assessed with the recast.

## The programs on which a recast is not offered

FHA, VA and adjustable loans cannot be recast. Borrowers on those programs may still make extra principal payments, which shorten the loan instead.

## Worked figures on hypothetical inputs

Take a loan on a program whose curtailment total is $10000.00, last recast two years ago, that is active and current. Since that recast the borrower has made extra principal payments whose principal parts were $4000.00, $2500.00 and $3500.00. Those parts total $10000.00, which is at least the program's curtailment total, so the curtailment condition is satisfied and the program's recast fee is assessed with the recast.

Had the three parts totalled $9800.00, the total would fall short of the $10000.00 the program states, and the curtailment condition would not be satisfied.

An extra principal payment made before that last recast does not enter the total, the total being measured from the date of the last recast.
